label: Forest
_model: The wild kernel: the APPETITE belongs to the place itself. A wood wants to be entered, fed, spread, or left uncounted, and the ACCOMMODATION is what it did to whoever was here — took them, grew through them, let them wander. Claimants are the wood's own names for itself.

appetites.want: to be walked into and never out of
appetites.purpose: nobody would ever find the far side
appetites.asks: "Which way did you think you were going?"

appeasement.move: walk in deliberately, and say aloud that you mean to

appetites.want: to be given something at the edge
appetites.purpose: nobody would ever pass without paying

appeasement.move: leave something of value at a root, without asking anything
appeasement.why: the wood has been given something

appetites.want: to grow over everything that was ever cleared

appeasement.move: let something of yours be taken and grown over
appeasement.why: the wood has taken back a little more

appetites.want: never to be mapped or measured
appetites.purpose: nobody would ever say how big it is

appeasement.move: admit aloud that you are lost, and mean it
appeasement.why: nobody can say where they are

accommodations.text: took {conscript} one at a time and did not give them back
grew through {conscript} until there was more wood than not
let {conscript} wander until they stopped wanting to leave
took {conscript} for a season and returned something else
kept {conscript} at the treeline, facing out, as a warning
let {conscript} put down roots where they stood

lantern.label: the lantern that still shows the way out
lantern.function: the only thing here that knows a direction

bowl.label: the bowl the offerings were left in
bowl.function: the only place the wood has ever been satisfied

axe.label: the axe that held the treeline for a century
axe.function: the only thing that ever cut and stayed cut

chain.label: a surveyor's chain, complete
chain.function: the only honest measurement anyone took

factions.name: the Taken
factions.essence: still walking the paths they were lost on

factions.name: charcoal-burners
factions.essence: working a wood that is working on them

factions.name: the Hunt
factions.essence: running something down, and has been for a long time

factions.name: what grew over the rest
factions.essence: neither knows nor cares who came through

triggerGlossary.announced: came in by the ride, singing or talking, as travellers do
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: passed the same tree twice, or were watched from two sides
triggerGlossary.loud: an axe, a shout, a horn — the wood minds all three
triggerGlossary.lingering: stopped moving long enough for the wood to catch up
triggerGlossary.disturbed: cut, broke or took something growing

skirmish.line: a Bat Swarm and 2 Giant Rats in the leaf-litter
skirmish.harmedBy: anything; fire scatters all of it
skirmish.avoid: stand still and they pass around you

foes.name: Dire Wolf
foes.note: circles; takes the one who runs

fight.avoid: nobody runs and they will not commit

battle.line: 1 Troll under the roots and 2 Dire Wolves

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: regrows unless the wound is burned

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire closes the wound
battle.avoid: it is territorial and will not follow past the treeline

nightmare.line: the Hunt: 1 Wraith mounted, 1 Troll and 4 Dire Wolves

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; fire for the Troll; anything for the wolves
nightmare.avoid: the Hunt passes over anyone standing perfectly still — say so before initiative

paths.dangerLine: the wood is still taking people in, and it is patient about it

institution: a ride cut straight for a mile and going nowhere
waymarks nailed to trees, all of them facing inward
a stile into the wood with no stile out
ritual: boots left in a row at the treeline, toes pointing in
a path swept clear of leaf-fall by nothing at all
a lantern lit at dusk on a post with no road
demand: a path that widens invitingly wherever you slow down
a clearing you keep arriving at from different directions
a track that is easier walking than the way back
wound: one boot, worn through, a long way from any road
waymarks prised off and stacked at a root
a track worn deep by someone walking it for years
anchor: a lantern still burning on a post at a crossway
a walking-staff planted upright, worn to the grain
a map-case, empty, hanging on a branch

features: a fresh blaze cut into bark, this season
a campfire cold but recent, with nobody's gear taken
a hat on a branch at head height
a path that was not there when you looked before
a coat folded neatly at a root
cart-ruts leading in and none leading out

decisions.cue: two paths, one plainly easier walking than the other
decisions.cost: the wood made one of them easy on purpose

resolve.success: you read the leaf-fall and take the true path, losing no time
resolve.failure: you take the easy path and it costs a Turn more than it should
resolve.orElse: take the hard path deliberately: one Turn, but you know where you are

decisions.cue: a lantern burning on a post at a crossway
decisions.cost: carrying it means the wood can see you coming

resolve.success: you take it and it shows the way — the party does not stray this delve
resolve.failure: you take it and something starts walking toward the light
resolve.orElse: leave it burning: no guidance, and no attention

decisions.cue: waymarks prised off and stacked at a root
decisions.cost: resetting them is a service to whoever comes next

resolve.success: you reset them and the Taken are grateful — they will guide you once
resolve.failure: you are seen doing it and the wood closes a path behind you
resolve.orElse: leave them stacked; you are not the wood's problem to solve

decisions.cue: a stranger's coat folded at a root, still dry
decisions.cost: taking it is theft from someone probably still walking

resolve.success: you find the mark inside and learn who is still on these paths
resolve.failure: you take it and something begins following at coat-distance
resolve.orElse: leave it folded; you will pass it again

decisions.cue: a clearing you have now arrived at twice
decisions.cost: the third time will not be a coincidence

resolve.success: you break the loop by leaving a mark and walking off it
resolve.failure: you arrive a third time: lose a Turn and roll the clock
resolve.orElse: walk out in a straight line whatever the ground does: one Turn, hard going

decisions.cue: a track worn deep by long use, going the wrong way
decisions.cost: following it finds whoever wore it

resolve.success: you follow it and find them, and they can still be spoken to
resolve.failure: you follow it and join it — the party walks it a Turn before noticing
resolve.orElse: ignore it; the walker keeps walking

situations.doing: walking a path it has walked for a very long time
situations.onArrival: it falls into step beside you without a word
situations.because: it was never told it could stop
situations.offer: tell it the way out and it will show you a shortcut in return

situations.doing: burning steadily with nothing to burn
situations.onArrival: the flame turns toward you as you approach
situations.because: it was lit for someone who never came
situations.offer: carry it and the paths behave for one area

situations.doing: recutting a blaze the wood keeps growing over
situations.onArrival: they nod and keep working
situations.because: the marks must be kept or the burn cannot be found
situations.offer: help them cut and they will mark your route out

situations.doing: standing at a fork, each facing a different way
situations.onArrival: they both turn to you to settle it
situations.because: they disagreed once and have not moved since
situations.offer: choose a path for them and both will walk it with you

situations.doing: widening ahead of you into easy walking
situations.onArrival: the going becomes noticeably pleasant
situations.because: the wood is being welcoming
situations.offer: refuse the easy way aloud and the wood respects it

situations.doing: standing upright where it was planted
situations.onArrival: the leaves around it are undisturbed
situations.because: whoever planted it meant to come back
situations.offer: take it up and the wood counts you a traveller, not a trespasser

temptations.cue: a lantern that burns without fuel
temptations.benefit: the party never loses its way
temptations.standingDrawback: everything in the wood knows where you are

temptations.cue: a waymark prised off a tree
temptations.benefit: once, make a path lead where you say
temptations.standingDrawback: the path you displaced has to go somewhere

temptations.cue: a walking-staff worn to the grain
temptations.benefit: once, walk out of anywhere in a straight line
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot stop walking while you hold it

temptations.cue: a boot-lace from the row at the treeline
temptations.benefit: once, retrace your steps exactly, however far
temptations.standingDrawback: you retrace someone else's too

temptations.cue: an empty map-case, oiled
temptations.benefit: once, know the way to somewhere you have never been
temptations.standingDrawback: the wood learns where you wanted to go

tithe.dangerLine: the wood is owed something, and it remembers who has not paid

institution: a stone at the treeline worn hollow by things set down on it
offerings nailed to a trunk at every height
a bowl at a root, never quite empty
ritual: bread left out, untouched but not stale
a first cut of every coppice stacked and unburned
a horn sounded at the edge before anyone enters
demand: a root grown across the path at exactly waist height
a hollow in a trunk at the height of an outstretched hand
a clearing where everything you carry feels heavier
wound: offerings taken back, and the trees around them dead
a bowl smashed and the pieces kept in place
a treeline that has moved a field's width since the wall was built
anchor: the offering-bowl itself, at the oldest root
a stone table with a hollow worn in the centre
a hoard of small given things in a hollow trunk

features: a fresh offering, still wet
a hollow tree stuffed with things nobody wanted
bread on a stone, untouched and not old
a coin pressed into bark and grown half over
a dead animal laid out deliberately, not eaten
a stack of first-cuttings, unburned

decisions.cue: a bowl at a root that is not quite empty
decisions.cost: leaving something is cheap; taking something is not

resolve.success: you leave something well-chosen and the wood eases — no clock roll in this area
resolve.failure: you leave something worthless and it is noticed: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave nothing and walk on; the wood keeps count

decisions.cue: a hollow trunk full of small given things
decisions.cost: one of them is exactly what you need

resolve.success: you take one and leave one, and the exchange is accepted
resolve.failure: you take without leaving, and the wood follows you the rest of the delve
resolve.orElse: take nothing: the need goes unmet

decisions.cue: a root grown across the path at waist height
decisions.cost: stepping over is trespass; going under is submission

resolve.success: you go under, which the wood counts as courtesy, and it lets you by
resolve.failure: you step over and the wood treats you as a woodsman from here
resolve.orElse: cut it: loud, roll the clock, and the wood remembers the cut

decisions.cue: a dead animal laid out deliberately at a crossway
decisions.cost: it was left for something that has not come

resolve.success: you read what it was left for, and what that thing wants instead
resolve.failure: you disturb it and whatever it was for arrives hungry
resolve.orElse: leave it and go round: one Turn

decisions.cue: bread on a stone, fresh, in a wood with nobody in it
decisions.cost: eating it accepts the wood's hospitality

resolve.success: you eat and are a guest — the Taken will not touch you this delve
resolve.failure: you eat and are fed by the wood, which means you belong to it: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: do not eat; you stay hungry and free

decisions.cue: a coin pressed into bark and half grown over
decisions.cost: prising it out takes back an offering

resolve.success: you free it cleanly and the tree does not seem to mind
resolve.failure: the bark tears and the wood takes something of yours instead
resolve.orElse: leave it; it will be gone entirely in another century

situations.doing: leaving bread on a stone and backing away from it
situations.onArrival: they gesture at you to be quiet, and to wait
situations.because: the tithe must be left and not watched
situations.offer: wait with them and they will share what the wood accepts

situations.doing: filling with rainwater that is not rain
situations.onArrival: the surface stills as you approach
situations.because: the bowl must not be empty
situations.offer: put something in it and the wood grants you one passage unmolested

situations.doing: carrying an armful of small things toward a hollow trunk
situations.onArrival: it offers you the armful to hold
situations.because: the offerings must be collected and never are
situations.offer: help it carry and it will let you keep one

situations.doing: stacking a first-cutting that will not be burned
situations.onArrival: they hand you an axe, handle first
situations.because: the first cut is owed and they cannot bring themselves to burn it
situations.offer: burn it for them and the wood counts the debt paid

situations.doing: closing a little around a stone with nothing on it
situations.onArrival: the gap you came through narrows
situations.because: something was due and was not left
situations.offer: leave anything at all and the gap opens

situations.doing: sounding at the treeline behind you
situations.onArrival: the note holds far longer than a horn should
situations.because: nobody announced themselves on the way in
situations.offer: answer it — shout back — and the wood treats you as expected

temptations.cue: a shallow bowl worn smooth at the rim
temptations.benefit: leave anything in it and the wood is satisfied, once
temptations.standingDrawback: it must be filled again before you leave the wood

temptations.cue: a ring from the hollow trunk, someone's offering
temptations.benefit: once, be owed a favour by something in the wood
temptations.standingDrawback: whoever gave it originally still wants it

temptations.cue: a bundle of first-cutting, unburned
temptations.benefit: once, burn it to buy safe passage for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: the smoke tells the wood exactly where you are

temptations.cue: bread from the offering-stone, still soft
temptations.benefit: eat it and nothing in the wood will touch you
temptations.standingDrawback: you are fed by the wood, and it counts you as its own

temptations.cue: a coin half grown into bark
temptations.benefit: once, pay a debt you have not the means to pay
temptations.standingDrawback: the tree it came from is looking for it

reclaiming.dangerLine: the wood is taking the ground back, and it does not stop while you watch

institution: a field wall with trees growing out of the top of it
furrows still visible under twenty years of bramble
a gate standing on its own with wood on both sides
ritual: coppice stools cut on a rotation nobody is keeping
a hedge laid by hands, thirty years ago, still holding
boundary trees marked and the marks grown shut
demand: a clearing that is smaller than it was this morning
saplings standing in a doorway in a line
a path narrowing behind you as you walk it
wound: a plough left in a furrow with a tree through it
a cottage with the roof gone and an oak in the hearth
an orchard gone feral, the grafts thrown off
anchor: an axe in a stump, handle still sound
a hedging bill hung on a nail in a wall that is now a tree
a ring of stumps cut clean, and nothing regrown

features: a wall pushed over from the wood side, recently
a sapling in a doorway, this year's growth
a plough share polished by roots
a fence post with a living branch
a chimney standing alone in a thicket
a wheel-rut with a tree in the middle of it

decisions.cue: a clearing that is measurably smaller than the map says
decisions.cost: the wood will not stop while you are watching it

resolve.success: you mark the edge and can tell how fast it is moving, which is useful
resolve.failure: you lose the edge and the clearing closes a little around you
resolve.orElse: move through fast and do not measure: one Turn, no knowledge

decisions.cue: an axe standing in a stump, handle sound
decisions.cost: using it is a declaration; leaving it is a concession

resolve.success: you cut what needs cutting and the ground stays open behind you
resolve.failure: the cut does not take and the wood closes the way you came: lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: leave the axe; the way narrows but nothing is provoked

decisions.cue: a cottage with an oak growing in the hearth
decisions.cost: what is inside was never cleared out

resolve.success: you get in and out through the roots, and find what was left
resolve.failure: the roots shift and the doorway closes: +1 Bane and a Turn to dig out
resolve.orElse: leave it; whatever is inside stays inside

decisions.cue: a hedge laid by human hands, still holding, blocking the way
decisions.cost: breaking it undoes a good piece of work

resolve.success: you find the layer's gap and pass without breaking a stem
resolve.failure: you force through and the hedge is ruined: the wood counts it
resolve.orElse: go round the hedge: two Turns

decisions.cue: saplings standing in a doorway in a deliberate line
decisions.cost: pulling them is easy and will be noticed

resolve.success: you pull them cleanly and replant them outside — the wood accepts the trade
resolve.failure: you pull them and drop them: the wood takes something of yours in exchange
resolve.orElse: step over them; the doorway is half closed and you are half through

decisions.cue: an orchard gone feral, and one tree still bearing
decisions.cost: the fruit is good and it is not yours

resolve.success: you take fruit in a way the orchard permits, and are the better for it
resolve.failure: you take too much and the orchard remembers the hand
resolve.orElse: take none: you go hungry and unremarked

situations.doing: cutting back a hedge that grew again behind them
situations.onArrival: they do not look up, and ask if you have a bill-hook
situations.because: the hedge must be kept and cannot be
situations.offer: cut with them and they will tell you where the old road ran

situations.doing: standing in a doorway in a straight line
situations.onArrival: the line shifts, very slightly, as you look at it
situations.because: the doorway is being closed
situations.offer: step through and say aloud that you are passing, and they let you

situations.doing: laying a hedge with hands that are mostly root
situations.onArrival: it holds out a stem for you to bend
situations.because: the work was begun and must be finished
situations.offer: bend the stem and it will lay you a gap through anything

situations.doing: closing by a hand's breadth while you stand in it
situations.onArrival: the light changes
situations.because: nothing cleared is permitted to stay cleared
situations.offer: cut one sapling and the clearing holds for the delve

situations.doing: dropping fruit in front of you as you pass
situations.onArrival: the fruit lands and does not roll
situations.because: the trees were tended once and remember it
situations.offer: eat, and the orchard will show you where the house was

situations.doing: arguing over a coppice stool cut out of rotation
situations.onArrival: they appeal to you as a third opinion
situations.because: the rotation was lost and the wood is taking the difference
situations.offer: settle it and they will burn a path for you

temptations.cue: an axe with a sound handle
temptations.benefit: once, cut a way through anything growing
temptations.standingDrawback: the wood counts every cut you make and settles later

temptations.cue: a hedging bill, oiled
temptations.benefit: once, close a way behind you that nothing follows through
temptations.standingDrawback: the way stays shut for you too

temptations.cue: a graft from the last bearing tree
temptations.benefit: once, make something grow where it should not
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you grow is the wood's, not yours

temptations.cue: a boundary stone the wood has not yet swallowed
temptations.benefit: once, hold a piece of ground against the wood for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: the wood takes twice that ground afterwards

temptations.cue: an iron share off a buried plough
temptations.benefit: once, break new ground and have it stay broken
temptations.standingDrawback: the wood knows there is iron in the party

trackless.dangerLine: the wood will not be counted, and it notices anyone trying

institution: survey pegs driven in rows and every one at a different angle
a chain hung in a tree, complete, at head height
cairns built to mark a line that does not run straight
ritual: a perambulation walked yearly and never finishing
a tally cut into a post, the count restarting
a rope measured out and coiled and measured again
demand: ground that is longer walking than looking
a stand of trees that is not the same number twice
a distance that changes depending which way you go
wound: a map torn into strips and nailed to six trees
a surveyor's theodolite smashed against its own tripod
a chain snapped and the links scattered along a mile
anchor: a surveyor's chain, complete and coiled
a field-book with the last page filled in a shaking hand
a cairn with a brass plate under the top stone

features: survey pegs pulled and re-driven wrongly
a tally-post with the count started over
a rope coiled at a root, measured and unmeasured
a cairn built this season
a page of a field-book pinned to bark
chain-links scattered in a line through the leaf-litter

decisions.cue: a surveyor's chain hung complete in a tree
decisions.cost: measuring anything here is the one thing the wood minds

resolve.success: you measure one distance honestly and it holds — you can trust that route
resolve.failure: the measurement comes out different twice and you lose a Turn to it
resolve.orElse: leave the chain hanging: no measurements, no offence

decisions.cue: a field-book with the last entry in a shaking hand
decisions.cost: reading it tells you what the surveyor found

resolve.success: you read it and learn one true thing about the wood's shape
resolve.failure: you read it aloud, and the wood hears itself described: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; the finding stays lost

decisions.cue: cairns marking a line that does not run straight
decisions.cost: following the cairns is following someone else's error

resolve.success: you spot where the line was corrected and follow the true one
resolve.failure: you follow the error and arrive somewhere you did not intend
resolve.orElse: ignore the cairns entirely: one Turn, your own reckoning

decisions.cue: a stand of trees you have counted twice and got two answers
decisions.cost: counting a third time is a challenge

resolve.success: you accept aloud that it cannot be counted, and the stand lets you through
resolve.failure: you insist on a number and the stand does not open: lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: do not count; walk through without looking too hard

decisions.cue: a map torn into strips and nailed to six trees
decisions.cost: assembling it is possible and slow

resolve.success: you assemble enough of it to know where the far side is
resolve.failure: you assemble it wrongly and are confidently mistaken for a Turn
resolve.orElse: take one strip and go: you know a fragment, and no more

decisions.cue: a perambulation the Taken are still walking, and a gap in the line
decisions.cost: joining the walk means walking it to the end

resolve.success: you join, walk one leg, and are let out at a place you chose
resolve.failure: you join and the walk does not end where you hoped: lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: let them pass: they nod, and the wood notes that you did not join

situations.doing: measuring the same distance for the fourth time
situations.onArrival: it asks you to hold the far end of a chain
situations.because: the survey must close and has never closed
situations.offer: hold the chain and it will tell you the one distance it trusts

situations.doing: standing in a number that is not the same twice
situations.onArrival: the count you began comes out differently
situations.because: the wood will not be enumerated
situations.offer: stop counting aloud and the stand opens

situations.doing: walking a perambulation with a gap in the line where someone dropped out
situations.onArrival: it beckons you into the gap
situations.because: the bounds must be walked by a full company
situations.offer: walk one leg with them and they will set you down wherever you name

situations.doing: tearing up their own map, carefully, into strips
situations.onArrival: they offer you a strip without explanation
situations.because: the map was wrong and they would rather it were nowhere
situations.offer: take the strip and it shows one true thing

situations.doing: standing where no cairn was a moment ago
situations.onArrival: the top stone is warm
situations.because: the line must be marked and the line keeps moving
situations.offer: add a stone and the cairns lead you somewhere useful, once

situations.doing: carrying a count that has restarted many times
situations.onArrival: the fresh cut is very fresh
situations.because: something is still counting and cannot finish
situations.offer: cut the next tally yourself and the wood accepts the number

temptations.cue: a surveyor's chain, complete
temptations.benefit: once, know a true distance in the wood
temptations.standingDrawback: the wood knows you measured it

temptations.cue: a field-book with one honest page
temptations.benefit: once, know exactly where you are
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot be lost, and the wood dislikes that

temptations.cue: a brass plate from under a cairn
temptations.benefit: once, fix a place so it stays where it is
temptations.standingDrawback: everything around that place moves instead

temptations.cue: a strip of a torn map
temptations.benefit: once, find the far side of anything
temptations.standingDrawback: the rest of the map wants to be reassembled

temptations.cue: a section of tally-post
temptations.benefit: once, make a count come out the same twice
temptations.standingDrawback: something begins counting you
